definition: Eyewitness memory is memory for an event a person has seen and later reports in testimony. In this context, it includes the details recalled about the witnessed event, including central and more peripheral information.

reasons: The packet supports eyewitness memory as testimony about a witnessed event and the inclusion of peripheral details, but it does not support the added claim about central information.

The definition adds a broader memory description (“memory for an event a person has seen and later reports in testimony”) that is only partially grounded in the packet’s wording about testimonies about a witnessed event; the packet does not define the term as such.
The packet does not explicitly define “eyewitness memory” as “memory for an event a person has seen and later reports in testimony.”

While the packet mentions “eyewitness testimonies” after viewing a video and relates a measure to “peripheral” details, it does not support the specific claim that this definition “includes…central and…peripheral information.”
The packet provides context and study findings about peripheral details in testimonies, but it does not provide an overall definitional characterization matching all parts of the proposed definition.
